model_note.S:
CC: My right shoulder hurts when I reach overhead.

HPI: 46-year-old female. Five weeks of right shoulder pain after ceiling painting. Lateral shoulder and proximal upper-arm pain. Shoulder ache remains proximal to elbow; occasional thumb tingling with neck stiffness. Aching with pain during elevation. 5/10; limits overhead reach and hair washing. Worse with overhead use and lying on right side. Morning stiffness approximately 10 minutes. No fall or sudden injury. Neck rotation can reproduce thumb tingling, not the principal shoulder pain. Relief with rest and warmth. Partial relief with acetaminophen 500 mg once or twice on workdays. No previous shoulder episode; intermittent neck ache for 1 year.

PMH: Type 2 diabetes for 8 years; reported A1c 7.2% 3 months ago.

PSH: Cesarean delivery 18 years ago.

Meds: Metformin 1000 mg twice daily; acetaminophen as above.

SH: Never smoked. One or two glasses of wine monthly. No recreational drugs. House painter; temporary modified duties available. Lives with teenage son; lifting help available.

FH: Mother: rheumatoid arthritis in her 50s. Father: hypertension; sister: no known major illness.

Allergies: Naproxen: hives and lip swelling; avoids NSAIDs.

ROS: Musculoskeletal: Joint pain limited to the right shoulder. No reported joint swelling. No generalized myalgia. Neurologic: No persistent numbness. Intermittent brief thumb paresthesia. No grip weakness; elevation pain-limited. General: No fever. No weight loss. No unusual fatigue.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 128/78 mmHg, P 72 bpm, R 16 rpm, T 98.4 F oral, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 6", Wt 172 lbs

General: Alert and comfortable at rest.
Musculoskeletal: No shoulder deformity, erythema or visible swelling. Tenderness over the right greater tuberosity and lateral shoulder; no acromioclavicular point tenderness. Right active shoulder elevation painful from 70 to 120 degrees; passive flexion nearly full with mild end-range discomfort. External rotation mildly limited by discomfort; left shoulder motion full. Right shoulder elevation and external rotation 4+/5 with pain; elbow, wrist and grip strength 5/5 bilaterally.
Neck: Mildly reduced cervical rotation to the right with neck discomfort.
Neurologic: Light touch intact in both upper limbs, including thumbs.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Osteopathic: C5 right paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
P: 1. Use temporary modified overhead duties and a physical-therapy/home mobility program; acetaminophen is an option after safe-dose review. Avoid NSAIDs pending allergy assessment because of hives/lip swelling. Reassess in 3 weeks; consider radiograph or ultrasound for persistent pain or objective weakness. New weakness, fever or a hot swollen joint needs earlier assessment.
2. If neck/arm symptoms persist, repeat focused neurologic assessment and consider cervical imaging/referral if deficits or progression develop. Explain safe work posture and gentle mobility.

3. If passive stiffness progresses, reassess for capsulitis and discuss stretching/physical therapy; consider specialist-guided injection with glucose counseling if indicated. Review diabetes management and explain how to monitor progressive stiffness.
